source.title: Regulation of parkinsonian motor behaviours by optogenetic control of basal ganglia circuitry.

confidence_rationale: Causal, pathway-specific manipulation showing D2/indirect and D1/direct populations drive opposite, dissociable motor phenotypes (freezing/bradykinesia vs locomotion) -- the population-level substrate for ARC-109 leg (ii). Mapping is moderate: optogenetic drive is not a dopamine-gain lesion, and the phenotype is motor, not selection among candidates.
failure_signatures: Bulk optogenetic excitation of a whole pathway is not the same manipulation as ARC-109's asymmetric dopamine-gain lesion (d2_da_gain), so the phenotype cannot be read as a prediction for that knob directly.
The paper tests gross motor output, not the conflict-versus-indifference selection distinction that is ARC-109's leg (i).

mapping.source_claim_statement: Bilateral optogenetic excitation of indirect-pathway (D2) striatal MSNs produces a parkinsonian state (freezing, bradykinesia, fewer locomotor initiations); excitation of direct-pathway (D1) MSNs reduces freezing, increases locomotion, and rescues these deficits in a dopamine-depleted Parkinson's model.
mapping.ree_translation: Causal evidence that the two populations are behaviourally dissociable and push in opposite directions -- the precondition for ARC-109's leg (ii): an asymmetric D2-side lesion should produce an akinesia/perseveration-like signature (fewer action initiations, longer commit runs) that is not produced by scaling a single additive accumulator by the same amount.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Optogenetic drive of a whole population is an activity manipulation, not a change in dopamine sensitivity; mapping it onto a d2_da_gain lesion assumes the two produce the same effective shift in the No-Go population's output. REE also has no registered disorder-analog readout for leg (ii) yet, so the phenotype has no instrument to land on.
mapping.source_context: D1-Cre and D2-Cre BAC transgenic mice, Cre-dependent ChR2 in dorsomedial striatum, open-field motor behaviour, 6-OHDA dopamine-depletion model.

confidence_components.notes: High-quality causal rodent study; mapping reduced because the manipulation and readout differ from the claim's lesion and selection DV.
